types.name: TextureArrayManifest
types.description: Serialized `*.textureArray` file. Layer order is the layer index.

types.name: TextureArrayLayer
types.description: One layer entry: a texture's uuid, a colour for a swatch, or a sheet to cut up.

types.name: TextureArraySlice
types.description: A sheet cut into one layer per cell, in reading order: across, then down. Every cell becomes a layer, so a frame is a layer index.

types.name: TextureArrayCell
types.description: Where a layer sits in the sheet it was cut from.

types.name: TileRef
types.description: Which tile an object renders: a layer index, or a layer texture's uuid.

types.name: PatchContributor
types.description: One owner of a material's shader hook, however many systems want to patch it. `material.onBeforeCompile` is a single slot and assigning it is last-one-wins, so two systems that patch the same material - texture arrays and cascaded shadows, say - would each silently disable the other, and a game that patches a shader of its own would disable both. This module keeps the list. The rules it enforces: - The material's own hook always runs first. Whatever was in the slot when the first system attached is kept as the base, whether that is a game's patch, a loader's, or a third party's. - Anything assigned to the slot later is adopted as the new base and stacked underneath, so an assignment made after the fact is repaired rather than obeyed. The comparison is on the function's source, which is also what three keys programs by, so a fresh closure with an unchanged body is not a change and recompiles nothing. - Contributors run in `order`, lowest first, so the result does not depend on which system loaded first. - `customProgramCacheKey` is composed from every contributor's `key()`, plus the base's. three caches compiled programs by that string, so a contributor whose output depends on a setting has to say so in `key()` or two materials can be handed each other's program. A contributor is a plain object and can be removed without touching the others.

types.name: CascadedShadowSettings
types.description: Cascaded shadow maps for a directional light, as an opt-in per light. Splits the lit area by distance, so the near slice gets a dense map and the far one a coarse map. `maxFar` is where the shadows stop, faded out rather than cut off. Wraps three's `three/examples/jsm/csm/CSM` rather than copying it: - Its constructor patches the global `ShaderChunk` and its `dispose` does not restore them, so the chunks are captured before the first set and put back when the last one goes. - Its `setupMaterial` would take over `material.onBeforeCompile`; the per-material half is a `ShaderPatch` contributor instead, and the uniforms are shared per frame. - Its cascade lights own the lighting, so they carry the real light's colour, intensity and direction, and no other directional light may cast a shadow while this is on - the chunk pairs light *i* with `CSM_cascades[i]` and with shadow map *i*. One light at a time: the shader composites a single cascade set.

types.name: PaletteTarget

types.name: BatchingMode

types.name: BoneHitPiece
types.description: Hit Mesh proxies. Splits a skinned mesh into RIGID invisible pieces — one per bone — that follow the bones, so projectiles/decals raycast them like any mesh: fast, pose-exact, and bullet holes ride the limb. Static meshes get one exact ghost clone. Public API is the `HitMesh` object. See project docs for the full workflow (generate → attach → rehydrate → HitSpot).
